name: Congenital Knee Dislocation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Knee Dislocation

criteria.description: Presence of hyperextension deformity of the knee at birth with inability to flex beyond neutral
Radiographic evidence of anterior displacement of the tibia relative to the femur
Presence of associated musculoskeletal anomalies such as ligamentous laxity or patellar hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical hyperextension deformity at birth plus radiographic confirmation of tibiofemoral dislocation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered if syndromic associations are suspected.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fixed hyperextension deformity of the knee
Anterior displacement of tibia relative to femur
searchTerms: tibia moved in front of thigh bone
forward displacement of lower leg bone

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inability to actively flex the knee beyond neutral position

common.symptomName: Ligamentous laxity around the knee joint

occasional.symptomName: Skin dimpling over the anterior knee

searchTerms: one limb shorter than the other

rare.symptomName: Neurovascular compromise of the distal limb
rare.notes: May occur due to severe dislocation or associated trauma
searchTerms: nerve and vessel problems in hand or foot
circulation and nerve issues in distal limb

rare.symptomName: Syndromic associations such as Larsen syndrome
Joint stiffness in adjacent joints (hip or ankle)

imaging: X-ray showing anterior displacement of tibia relative to femur
Ultrasound for soft tissue assessment in neonates
MRI for detailed ligament and cartilage evaluation if needed
genetic: Genetic testing for syndromic causes such as Larsen syndrome or other connective tissue disorders
other: Physical examination revealing fixed hyperextension deformity
Assessment of ligamentous laxity and muscle contractures

distinguishingFeatures: Multiple joint contractures involving upper and lower limbs
Radiographic findings consistent with acute injury

redFlags: Neurovascular compromise of the distal limb
Failure to achieve knee flexion with conservative management
references: Bensahel H, et al. Congenital dislocation of the knee: diagnosis and treatment. J Pediatr Orthop. 1990.
Orphanet: Congenital knee dislocation. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
Hunter JB, et al. Congenital knee dislocation: a review of the literature. J Pediatr Orthop B. 2016.
